name: Labourism
summary: Labourism is the politics of the trade-union-based labour movement: it seeks to defend and advance workers' interests, through collective bargaining and an independent labour party in Parliament, within the existing constitutional order. Its programme combined a national minimum standard of living, public ownership of key industries, steeply taxed wealth and a League-based internationalism, but it grew empirically out of unionism rather than from a revolutionary theory.
scope: The British Labour Party and trade-union tradition from the Labour Representation Committee (1900) to the post-1945 era, built on Keir Hardie's independent-labour politics, the Webbs' 1918 'Labour and the New Social Order' and Clause IV. It follows the sense of 'labourism' that contrasts it with socialism (defending labour within the system rather than changing it), and excludes Marxist socialism, the later Third Way and Christian labourism as a separate entry. Many social and foreign-policy questions were never addressed by the doctrine, so those answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: The 1918 constitution and programme: national minimum, nationalisation, taxation, League of Nations, trade-union federation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1918 national minimum and the 1940s NHS made tax-funded universal care a Labour hallmark; sources here describe the welfare-state aim rather than health care by name.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 1918 programme made a minimum wage the first pillar of the national minimum, with the figure revised as prices rose.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Common ownership and the progressive elimination of the private capitalist from industry rest on distrust of unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Clause IV of 1918 pledged common ownership of the means of production, and the programme named mines, railways and electric power for immediate nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1918 programme called for very steep taxes on the highest incomes (up to 16s or 19s in the pound) and a capital levy on wealth.

unions-good.rationale: Labourism is the political arm of trade unionism; Hardie praised the growing altruism of trade unions and the party began as the unions' parliamentary committee.

property-fundamental.rationale: Labourists accepted private property for personal use but committed the party to common ownership of industry, so overriding property rights was normal policy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Democratic control of industry and the national minimum imply tight public control of employers, beyond what the sources spell out for regulation as such.

cut-welfare.rationale: The movement's purpose was to secure a social minimum and protect labour; cutting welfare reverses the 1918 programme.

worker-ownership.rationale: Common ownership meant municipal or state ownership more often than worker cooperatives, and cooperatives were a minor strand, so adherents split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The sources never address surveillance; Labour has been split between civil-liberties and law-and-order wings.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; the unions' respectable, working-class culture and Labour's cautious social record suggest scepticism, inferred rather than documented.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Labour passed race-relations laws but labourism had no doctrine on speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement valued parliamentary and party discipline and collective union decision-making over bypassing institutions through a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: The 1918 programme treated the state as the nation's largest producing and distributing agency and extended it; wanting no state is the reverse.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Labour governments' firearms controls and a general preference for public order over gun rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: Labourism had no doctrine on policing; its governments funded both, while the left of the movement distrusted the use of police against strikers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the respectable moralism of the chapel and union tradition that Hardie's speech reflects.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1918 programme favoured elected local bodies as a check on bureaucracy, but its core aim of a national minimum needs national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the movement's reformist, humanitarian tradition and the later Labour abolition of the death penalty.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's culture was socially traditional but its programme prioritised wages and welfare, so adherents split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the historic movement; the union-chapel tradition was conservative while later Labour supported legal reform.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Labour governments passed the 1967 Act but the movement's Catholic and chapel members were divided.

more-religion-public.rationale: Hardie criticised ministers who backed harsh social dogmas, though nonconformity shaped the movement; not a doctrinal demand for public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the movement was formally anti-racist but defined its aims by class and nation rather than group redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; Hardie supported women's emancipation but labourism had no theory about gender construction.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nairn describes Labour as leaning towards British traditions, and labourism was patriotic and national in outlook; stated only indirectly.

gradual-change.rationale: Labourism, as Miliband and Nairn describe it, seeks social reform within existing institutions and Parliament, an ideology of adaptation rather than rupture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue; unions feared wage competition while Labour leaders opposed racial exclusion, so adherents were split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1918 programme backed a League of Nations and arbitration of disputes between states.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; early labourism sat with Liberal free-trade politics while later union interests favoured protection of jobs.

nation-first.rationale: The 1918 foreign policy rested on a League of Nations and arbitration rather than national self-assertion.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The historic movement was anti-militarist but Attlee-era Labour accepted force; no doctrine addresses humanitarian intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement that organised within the nation-state and union labour markets bounded by national law.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; labourism sought growth to fund wages and welfare, so limiting growth conflicts with its aims.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; unions with industry jobs at stake were divided on climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; labourism welcomed modernisation but protected workers from its costs.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from union support for industrial jobs and Labour's civil nuclear programme.

revolution-justified.rationale: Labourism is described as an ideology of adaptation within capitalism's framework and a party of Parliament, not of rupture.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Webbs brought expert administration into the party, but labourism rooted legitimacy in democratic and union mandate; adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: The 1918 programme nationalised key industries but kept a mixed economy, so labourism neither embraced full central planning nor rejected all planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Common ownership alongside continuing markets for goods in a mixed economy matches the programme; markets were never abolished.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Liberal land reform appealed to the movement but it was not central to Labour's programme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme's capital levy and steep taxation of wealth to fund the common good imply taxing large inheritances.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; labourism emphasised wages from work and a national minimum, so unconditional payment is inferred as unattractive.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split between free-trade tradition and union job protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1918 programme put the state in command of key industries and public works to reduce unemployment, implying public direction of investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Common ownership was the party's aim; widespread small ownership is a Liberal or distributist ideal that labourism did not adopt.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Labourism defends labour's interests within the existing wage system and seeks higher wages and conditions, not the abolition of wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme proposed a revolution in national finance under public control, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Labour-movement bargaining is traditionally voluntary between unions and employers, not through state-recognised bodies, though some countries use co-determination.

one-party-rule.rationale: Labourism worked through competitive parliamentary politics and the party sought to form a government by election, not to rule as a sole party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; the movement accepted the constitutional monarchy while republican sentiment existed on its left.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement was founded on winning workers political voice, and Hardie's speech ties freedom to democratic enfranchisement.

direct-votes.rationale: Labourism relied on parliamentary representation; referendums were not part of its programme.

workers-councils.rationale: Labour-movement politics ran through unions and Parliament; councils replacing parliaments are a revolutionary-socialist idea labourism opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was unionist about Britain while the 1918 programme backed self-government within the Empire.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hardie's movement existed to break down class barriers, and its democratic faith denies a natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Labourism sought change through bargaining and Parliament and rejected revolution, though the doctrine does not rule out all force.

war-builds-character.rationale: The 1918 programme rested on a League of Nations and arbitration; the movement saw war as a failure of the old order.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; nonconformist Christianity influenced the movement while secular and Anglican traditions also coexisted.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Hardie condemned dogmas upheld by clergymen, and the movement sought democratic legislation rather than scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme enlarged public responsibilities; privatising courts and defence has no place in labourism.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's internationalist peace aims sat alongside Attlee-era commitment to defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Labourism defined its constituency by class and Hardie spoke of breaking down class and sex barriers, not an ethnic nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nairn shows labourism growing from craft unions seeking to protect their interests within capitalism, without a theory of class conflict as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The national minimum and heavy taxation of surplus wealth for the common good aim at narrowing outcomes, though not at strict equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic for the historic movement; no stated position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The 1918 programme sought self-government within the Empire but not reparations; inferred as unsupported.

civilizational-union.rationale: Labourism's internationalism was through a universal League of Nations, not unions of nations defined by civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hardie contrasted the growing altruism of trade unionism with greed, a rejection of self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity language stressed mutual duty while the movement defended workers' rights.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; population control sat outside the doctrine and was resisted by many Labour Catholics.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Labourism emerged from industrial trade unionism and sought to share industry's gains, not reject industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; unions welcomed modernisation while resisting job losses.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's reliance on democratic and union accountability.

restore-past-order.rationale: The 1918 programme was a forward-looking reconstruction of the social order, and Hardie spoke of progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Eatwell and Wright's contrast has labourism pursuing labour's interests pragmatically within the system, and Nairn says the party arose empirically rather than from theory.

direct-action.rationale: Labourism favours parliamentary and bargaining routes, though unions use strikes when needed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between pragmatic and principled stances.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Labourism is an industrial-era movement for workers' share of industry's output.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Labourism organises workers within existing trades and industries; abolishing the division of labour is a utopian-Marxist idea.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The 1918 national minimum guarantees basic needs, but pay for work remained the general principle.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme's common ownership implies production serving social needs, but labourism rarely framed it this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Eatwell and Wright contrast labourism with socialism: it defends labour within capitalism without a theory that profit is exploitation, though unions seek a fairer share.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Labourism worked by parliamentary methods and Beer's account stresses the party's political, not dictatorial, struggle.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the urban, industrial base of labourism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The 1918 programme read the war as the collapse of capitalism's old order, but labourism did not adopt the doctrine that capitalism inevitably causes imperial wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme's central fiscal aim was steeply graduated taxation to fund the common good.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Labourism is organised around collective rights of workers and unions, so rejecting group rights sits ill with it.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed directly; labourists were split between pacifists and those who accepted wartime service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Labourism is a voice politics of organising and voting; exit as the main check is a libertarian idea.

state-as-business.rationale: Public ownership and services for citizens, not customers, are central to the 1918 programme.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hardie described the demand as economic freedom as the natural outcome of political enfranchisement, which treats freedom as requiring material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; labourism's grievances targeted employers and landed privilege, not universities or media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Hardie's movement rejected barriers of class and sex and the doctrine's egalitarian outlook rejects hereditary ability ranking by race.

organic-representation.rationale: Labourism relies on representation through unions and parties but within parliamentary elections, not through families and communities.

total-state.rationale: The party sought democratic control and elected local bodies to counter bureaucracy and centralisation, which rules out directing all areas of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 1918 programme sought reconstruction, but not a radical national rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The programme rejected forcible domination of other countries and favoured arbitration through a League.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Labourism is built on elected, constitutional democracy.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour contradicts a movement founded to defend workers' freedom and economic independence.

universal-morality.rationale: Hardie's appeals to altruism and Christian ethics suggest some belief in universal ideals, but the doctrine has no stated epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: The programme speaks of the surplus wealth for the common good, but labourism saw politics as representing labour's interests competing with others.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Labour-movement parties backed Israel after 1948 and Attlee-era Labour had Zionist sympathies; not a doctrinal position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the movement's core aims.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Labour movements pursue co-determination with worker board seats in some countries and the 1918 programme called for democratic control of industry.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme favoured public provision of education, with a school-leaving age of 16, over market-style vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme advocated public works schemes to reduce unemployment, which implies willingness to run deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hardie held that political freedom required economic freedom, but through collective means, so the claim's free-market sense is rejected.

rule-by-example.rationale: Labourism rests on democratic institutions and law, not on rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 1918 programme called for self-government within the Empire and rejected domination of other peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: The programme's League of Nations approach prefers collective authorisation to unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Hardie's Christian-socialist tone and the union-chapel tradition mix faith and reason; no doctrine.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed universal entitlement while unions were wary of labour-market competition.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The national minimum covered the sick, aged and unemployed, but the movement's work ethic also supported work as the norm.

class-collaboration.rationale: Labourism defends labour's interests through bargaining within the system, but Nairn shows unions set against employers, so adherents are split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; the statement is an idiosyncratic claim and labourism supported libraries and public culture as common goods.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; the programme favoured internationalism through the League over bloc-building among dominated states.

workers-nation.rationale: Labourism organised workers nationally through British unions and the Labour Party rather than internationally, as Nairn's account of its national growth shows.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hardie praised women's awakening and the party's 1918 constitution eased women's membership.

ban-interest.rationale: Lending at interest was not opposed in the programme, which proposed public control of finance rather than a ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement's egalitarian aims and opposition to racial domination rule out segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Labourism sees the state as a tool that labour can capture through elections, not as inherently a ruling-class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; the unions' coal base supported fossil industry while later movement is divided.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no place in a movement that blames capitalism and landed privilege.

proportional-representation.rationale: Labour long favoured first-past-the-post, which gave it single-party government; inferred rather than stated in sources.

national-mission.rationale: The programme sought a League of Nations and self-government within the Empire, not a mission to spread British government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Hardie's speech sees women's emancipation as important but labourism had no theory of structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Labourism distrusted old ruling classes and landed privilege but participated in the political system.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to the movement's egalitarian ethos, though some early socialists favoured eugenics.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programme extended state activity in industry, finance and welfare, the opposite of a limited night-watchman state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inference: the 1900-1950 movement did not address this; drawn from its egalitarian outlook, though early labour also had restrictionist currents.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hardie's speech describes breaking down sex and class barriers, which expresses equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Labourism sought gradual reform at home through Parliament and had no revolution to extend abroad.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; not a labourist issue.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement's liberal nonconformist roots oppose restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to the doctrine and inconsistent with its secular working-class character.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; Labour governments left church schools in place and the movement had both secular and Christian wings.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The party aimed at democratic control and elected local bodies, not a strengthened state to defend socialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Hardie and the movement demanded workers' participation through enfranchisement; Labour rested its claim on elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; mercantilist export drive is not part of labourism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; labourism has no libertarian non-aggression doctrine.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Hardie contrasted competitive greed with the altruism of trade unionism; labourism favours cooperation and solidarity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Labour's gradualist democracy favoured open competition, though Labour leaders also fought communist entryism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hardie's economic freedom and labour's defence against employer power fit the idea, though labourism did not use republican vocabulary.

separated-powers.rationale: Labourism trusted parliamentary sovereignty and electoral majorities rather than checks on them.

vanguard-party.rationale: Labourism formed the party from existing unions and Parliament's mass electorate; Beer describes it as a federation, not a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The national minimum for the lowest paid and the unemployed is the first pillar of the 1918 programme.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Labour opposed the 1980 Right to Buy policy in principle and kept council housing public; not in the sources opened.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour movements pursue strikes where necessary and labour law via government to protect unions, not to restrict them.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme blamed the distribution of wealth, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement defined belonging by class and common citizenship; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Labourism relied on elected parliamentary office; lotteries are foreign to it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; labourism accepted wartime powers while civil-libertarian members objected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The programme controlled prices of essentials implicitly through the national minimum and public control of key industries; wartime Labour accepted price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement valued free expression for workers, and a controlled press contradicts its democratic faith.

party-commands-army.rationale: Labourism accepted civil and parliamentary control of the armed forces, not a party army.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Early Labour demanded payment of MPs so workers could serve; the idea of pay near an average worker's fits the ethos, though not set out in opened sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Labour's origin in the union movement valued collective decisions and party discipline, though MPs often dissented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Labour's attitude to Europe swung between support and hostility; unclear for the historic movement.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; no stated position.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; nonconformists in the movement opposed episcopal control of the church.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement's democratic faith and Hardie's critique of clerical dogma exclude clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Some labourists opposed WWI and the movement split, but the mainstream backed the war effort.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's democratic liberalism despite chapel moralism.

recall-officials.rationale: Labourism rested on parliamentary representation and trustee MPs; recall was not a demand.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Attlee-era Labour built NATO, though the 1918 programme favoured a League; the mainstream accepted alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Labourism championed council and rented housing as public provision.

people-in-arms.rationale: The movement accepted professional armed forces under parliamentary control.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Labourism's base was urban industrial workers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; Nairn notes the party drew in middle-class intellectuals while distrusting them.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Hardie's egalitarianism is about people, not civilisations.

death-penalty.rationale: Labour governments and the movement abolished the death penalty in 1965; not addressed in opened sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Labour's later education policies.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a public-education tradition favouring standard science teaching.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; moralism and civil liberty both found in the movement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The movement's civic, class-based membership suggests residency-based citizenship; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; Welsh and Scottish Labour supported minority languages.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The 1918 programme was about national finance and a capital levy; foreign debt was not addressed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme's self-government within the Empire is political; economic decolonisation was not addressed.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Labourism worked within existing constitutional arrangements and Parliament.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement fought for political rights as the base of economic freedom.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Hardie's internationalism and altruism suggest support, inferred as the sources say little on aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Labour split over the bomb; Attlee built it while unilateralists opposed it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Labourism accepted the constitutional monarchy and parliamentary government.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The 1918 programme called for a revolution in national finance under democratic control.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Private property serving the common good through the programme's surplus wealth for the common good and common ownership of industry.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; labourists split between admirers of the Soviet experiment and anti-communists.

collective-defense.rationale: Attlee-era Labour led NATO's creation, though the historic movement's pacifist wing dissented; sources opened do not cover it.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed directly; the programme rejected forcible domination of other countries.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The movement accepted a constitutional monarch standing above party; not documented in opened sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts the movement's democratic and egalitarian foundations.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme demanded very steep taxes on the highest incomes, the opposite of a flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hardie's appeal to altruism and removal of greed reflect belief in social circumstances shaping people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contradicts the movement's democratic and constitutional faith.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's priorities were domestic welfare.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Labourism favoured an elected Parliament without privileged orders.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement valued collective union decision-making over personality cults.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Labourism has no revolutionary-socialist state and believed party leaders served democratic mandates.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme nationalised land in principle but did not seek redistribution to peasants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The programme rejected forcible domination of other countries.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts the movement's liberal and democratic ethos.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the movement's liberal and egalitarian ethos.

common-currency.rationale: Labour's attitude to European currency union was divided.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The programme's internationalism was universal, not based on language-family unions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Labourism stressed equal citizenship and organisation within existing states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Labourism arose empirically, without adopting Marxist historical materialism, per Nairn.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme sought democratic control of industry and elimination of private capitalists, which opposes concentrated private power.

no-bailouts.rationale: The programme's public works and state intervention in industry imply support for rescuing jobs; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Labour's tradition of parliamentary sovereignty favours majority will over judicial limits.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic for the historic movement; later Labour used all-women shortlists.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme's League internationalism opposes economic blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The labour movement seeks labour protections that cross borders and the 1918 programme embraced international institutions.

moral-incentives.rationale: Labourism fights for higher wages and material conditions as its core purpose.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Labourism is described as an ideology of adaptation within capitalism, not rupture.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Nairn shows labourism attacked landed privilege as a political theme, though it was less hostile to monarchy and the Lords.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on curriculum emphasis.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1918 programme rejected forcible domination of other races and countries and called for self-government within the Empire.

patriotic-education.rationale: The movement was patriotic but schools doctrine was not a labourist demand; adherents split.

public-money-creation.rationale: The programme's revolution in national finance under public control fits creating money through a public body, though it is not spelled out.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Labourism, as Eatwell and Wright contrast it, works inside capitalism to protect labour, assuming the system can be reformed rather than collapse.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme's League internationalism and Hardie's comradeship across nations oppose delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Nairn notes that craft unions protected skilled workers' privileges, but labourism does not treat workers as non-exploited.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inference: drawn from the movement's egalitarianism and its acceptance of law limiting owners' rights in the workplace; the sources do not discuss discrimination by private owners.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Labourism relied on parliamentary sovereignty rather than entrenched limits on majorities.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement was founded to win workers a vote and elected representation.

minority-veto.rationale: Labourism relied on majority decisions and party and union discipline, not minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; labourism was constitutionalist with no stated theory of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Beer shows the movement worked through Parliament and aimed to form governments there.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from humanitarian sentiments in the movement.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream view among adherents.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hardie criticised charity-style paternalism and labourism sought rights through organisation rather than the duty of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is about collective political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; critical theory is foreign to labourism.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; the programme's anti-imperialism targeted domination, not a world-system theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Contradicts the movement's civic, class-based egalitarianism.

party-own-road.rationale: The movement developed its own national, gradualist path, per Nairn's empirical origins.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Hardie's internationalism implies support for solidarity over pure self-reliance; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The programme rejected forcible domination of other countries.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Labour was anti-fascist in the 1930s-40s; not in opened sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Attlee and Bevin-era Labour were anti-communist and anti-fascist; not in opened sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Contradicts the movement's egalitarian and anti-slavery ethos.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The programme and Hardie's universal appeals assume common aims of democratic institutions across countries.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Labourism accepted civilian parliamentary control of the armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed by the historic movement; adherents are split.

office-by-exam.rationale: The movement valued elected office; Beer notes the Webbs brought expertise into the party, but exam-selected rule instead of elections is rejected.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from later Labour reforms and liberal sentiment.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Labourism used trustee-style parliamentary representation, though unions held MPs accountable to the movement.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The national minimum covers old-age payments through public provision rather than private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme nationalised land in principle, but practice stayed unclear.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The movement worked through Parliament, whose control of taxation is central to the constitution it relied upon.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Hardie condemned greed but labourism sought higher consumption for workers.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The League approach and rejection of domination are incompatible with arming insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The programme rejected forcible domination of other countries.

corporate-influence.rationale: Labourism existed to counter employers' power in politics, and the programme sought to eliminate private capitalist control of industry.

job-guarantee.rationale: The programme proposed public works to reduce unemployment, which falls short of a full guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: The League of Nations idea assumed peace through democratic and legal institutions; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Labourism works through law and Parliament.

non-intervention.rationale: The League idea allowed collective action, so strict non-intervention is not documented.

industrial-unions.rationale: Labour movements pursue sectoral bargaining, and Nairn contrasts craft unionism's narrow protection, but labourism included both forms.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no place in the movement.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; marriage reform was not a labourist demand.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The programme's democratic control of industry implies transparency; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; the movement valued industry and trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: Labourism organises through formal unions, branches and a parliamentary party rather than small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The programme backed the League but also parliamentary sovereignty; adherents split.

religious-nation.rationale: Labourism defined its constituency by class and citizenship.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The programme rejected domination in international relations.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: National redistribution through a national minimum requires pooling revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Common ownership applied to the means of production, not personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Attlee-era Labour was anti-communist while the early movement showed solidarity with Soviet Russia; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Common ownership and municipal control were the preferred mode for services, not a mix of private providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Hardie's movement drew on Christianity and nonconformity.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Labourism accepts capitalism as the given framework and does not offer a historical verdict.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hardie linked women's awakening to wider social change; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed by the historic movement; split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Irrelevant and contrary to the movement's practical outlook.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives were a minor strand while the movement worked through national parties and unions.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inference: settlement policy for minority regions was never a British labour question; drawn from the movement's egalitarian outlook.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Labourism contrasted itself with revolutionary socialism but accepted a mixed economy; adherents are split.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Labour governments decriminalised in 1967; inferred and not in opened sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement fought for free organisation and political rights.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Hardie's nonconformist liberal tradition opposed it; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The programme called for self-government within the Empire and no forcible domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable to the doctrine; no stated position.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contradicts the movement's democratic and constitutional basis.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Labourism relied on representative democracy but also union and branch participation; adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; treated as a conscience issue.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Labourism defines itself by representing labour against capital and as a distinct party of the labour movement.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist theory was not central to labourism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inference: the 1900-1950 movement did not address this; drawn from its egalitarian outlook, though early labour also had restrictionist currents.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Labour movements seek labour-law protection for workers against employers; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The national minimum plus a mixed economy matches combining markets with social protection, though labourism went further in public ownership.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Labourism accepted defence under parliamentary control.

rich-first.rationale: The programme's emphasis on the national minimum and taxing wealth opposes letting the rich grow first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement tolerated the constitutional monarchy; no doctrine.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The programme proposed public control of finance rather than mutual credit banks.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement's founding goal was enfranchising workers, whom property franchises excluded.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Labourism's critique of wealth's power suggests agreement; inferred and not documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutional lawmaking through Parliament underlies the movement.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contradicts the movement's democratic enfranchisement ethos.

open-government-data.rationale: Democratic control of industry suggests openness; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inference: British labour never addressed religious marriage law; restricting it is foreign to its secular-egalitarian outlook.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inference: not addressed by the movement; a religious boycott is foreign to its egalitarian outlook.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Hardie's critique of greed and the programme's taxing of wealth suggest agreement.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement drew on Christian and nonconformist traditions.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Labourism accepted the state's law-enforcement role.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The programme replaced charity with a statutory national minimum.

term-limits.rationale: Labourism used standard parliamentary careers; term limits were not a demand.

vote-delegation.rationale: Labourism relied on conventional elected representation.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Hardie's support for women's emancipation suggests agreement; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: The programme's broad public control of essentials and the later council-housing tradition suggest support; not stated in opened sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from labourism's acceptance of existing property law.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Contradicts the movement's democratic and voluntary character; no drilled youth movement is part of labourism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Labour split between multilateralists and unilateralists.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Labour was split by Attlee-era alliance with the US and later left opposition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Clause IV's phrase on securing workers the full fruits of their industry directly states the idea.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism was a strand but most adherents accept defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position, and Nairn sees Labour as a novelty.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; labour martyrs such as Tolpuddle were commemorated but the claim concerns saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Hardie's language was moral and religious, but the doctrine is practical.

culture-before-state.rationale: Labourism prioritised political and economic reform.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Contradicts the movement's civic egalitarian outlook.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement was union-founded and bargaining autonomy from state and party is a core trade-union principle, though affiliation to Labour tied them to a party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Labourism sought workers' influence through parliament and unions rather than workers' rule as defining socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The programme proposed municipalisation and public control of services.

second-chamber.rationale: Labourism criticised the House of Lords as a seat of privilege; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme combined municipal and national ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; labourism favoured national government.

family-wage.rationale: The programme's national minimum wage was framed to support a family and revised with prices.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Hardie's moral and religious language supports a spiritual view while the doctrine takes no position.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Parliamentary sovereignty implies devolved powers revocable by the national legislature.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: League of Nations arbitration and rejection of conquest suggest agreement.

communal-electorates.rationale: The movement rejected communal electorates for common citizenship.

free-public-college.rationale: The programme extended educational opportunity; free tuition is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Hardie praised women's awakening; no doctrine of distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: The League of Nations and arbitration aim implied reducing armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Labour's 1918 foreign policy assumed open League-based diplomacy; inferred from the League approach.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme's national finance revolution implies control over capital; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Labourism accepted the state's monopoly of arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Mainstream labourism backed the war effort despite pacifist strands.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The labour movement pursues collective and sectoral bargaining as its main tool.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not in the historic doctrine, which favoured wage floors; New Labour used credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inference: labour programmes called for public works and finance reform rather than borrowing limits, but the 1929-31 Labour government under Snowden held to fiscal orthodoxy, so opposition was not firm; legal rules were never proposed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The programme's finance revolution was national; no stated position on world economy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Labourism works through existing institutions and Parliament, per Eatwell and Wright's contrast.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nairn shows Labour inherited a traditional national outlook but labourism has no sacred-nation theory.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Hardie's altruism and universalism suggest agreement.

public-service-media.rationale: The programme's democratic public provision and the BBC tradition suggest agreement; not stated in opened sources.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Labour was split between multilateralists and unilateralists.

workers-own-party.rationale: Independent labour representation defined the movement; Nairn shows early unions' subordination to the Liberals as the thing it overcame, and Beer describes the party as the unions' parliamentary committee.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's equal-citizenship and welfare-state outlook that law should protect individuals.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the labour movement's support for equal citizenship and the 1918 programme's democratic aims.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The labour tradition never addressed how languages are classified.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the programme's reliance on public ownership and state regulation of industry rather than private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic parliamentary aim and its opposition to hereditary privilege; customary chiefs were never discussed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental protection was not part of the early doctrine; inferred collectivist leanings are offset by its priority on workers' economic interests.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reformist, rehabilitative outlook; the sources do not address sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The movement never settled this; unions feared wage competition but stressed solidarity and integration, so adherents are split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Closed shops and union strength were the movement's aim; inferred from its union base, not stated in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the movement's drive to widen the franchise and its distrust of barriers to voting.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from its constitutional-reform outlook and Nonconformist and secular strands.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Labourism pursues its aims through elections and Parliament within the existing constitutional order, as the summary and scope describe.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; early Labour mixed Nonconformist moralism with liberal attitudes, so adherents split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its defence of civil liberties and of union organising, which depends on open communication.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the national minimum delivered by public services and insurance, not by replacing welfare with a cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Labour and its leaders such as Hardie backed votes for women, in line with its democratic aims; the sources here do not treat it directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement that put class, not religion, at the root of oppression, and had Nonconformist members.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its universalist and internationalist egalitarianism.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its support for state action to secure equal standards, such as the national minimum.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Labour's programme treated land and key resources as subject to public ownership rather than first-claim title.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the League-based internationalism in the programme; international courts are anachronistic here.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the movement drew on Nonconformist ethics but made no doctrinal claims about scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the labour movement's support for women's equality; self-government was not addressed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: labourism was constitutional and non-revolutionary, and early Labour was split over the Soviet state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to parliamentary democracy under the constitutional order.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from Nonconformist and labour support for disestablishment; adherents varied.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its self-determination and Home Rule sympathies; not addressed directly.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from League internationalism and self-determination; not addressed directly.

simple-living.rationale: Never addressed; the programme aimed at a rising standard of living, not asceticism.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its protection of vulnerable peoples; not addressed by the doctrine.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: Labour and the unions were split on conscription, so no settled view.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from labourism's class and internationalist focus, which puts workers' interests ahead of national spiritual themes.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the labour movement's constitutional, rights-based politics, which does not allow killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Never addressed by the doctrine; labour internationalism is not tied to either power, so inferred as split.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from labourism's focus on workers within its own constitutional order, with no kin-state tradition.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Clause IV's common ownership and the 1918 programme's taxation of wealth, which treat natural wealth as a common claim.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the collectivism of trade unionism and the national minimum, which place solidarity over individual self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the 1918 programme, which raised revenue by steeply taxing wealth and surplus income rather than by taxing everyday goods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The 1918 national minimum was meant for all citizens as a universal standard rather than means-tested relief.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Labourism works through the unions and the labour party as the link between workers and government, so bypassing them contradicts it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the labour movement's hostility to privileged capital and to special advantages for employers.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from labourism's class-based organisation, which cut across religious lines, though it had Nonconformist roots.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed by labourism; inferred as split between those who prize tradition and those who prize modernisation.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Hardie's opposition to sex barriers and labour's equality aims.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the 1918 programme of public ownership of key industries, which puts national resources under national control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The 1918 programme of a national minimum and steeply taxed wealth treats unequal outcomes as a matter of justice, not just of how wealth was gained.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not in the sources; inferred from the programme's steep taxation of wealth and later Labour support for taxing speculative finance.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; inferred from the movement's class focus and its later anti-discrimination stance that racism remains an obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from labourism's constitutional, parliamentary method, which works through changing laws rather than treating them as void.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the movement's aim of shorter hours and shared gains of industry; not discussed by name in the sources.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the League-based internationalism in the 1918 programme, which favoured global institutions over a balance of powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Clause IV of the 1918 constitution secures to workers the full fruits of their industry, which presupposes that labour creates the value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Hardie's and the unions' rootedness in national working-class life; sources describe working-class politics within the constitutional order.

material-over-identity.rationale: Labourism defends workers' interests through bargaining and wages first; identity politics came later, so this is inferred from its focus.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Labourism seeks change within the constitutional order and distinguished itself from Marxist socialism; inferred as rejecting party-led one-party systems.

missingStatements.text: Working people should have their own political party, independent of the established parties.
missingStatements.rationale: Independent labour representation defined the movement; Nairn shows early unions' subordination to the Liberals as the thing it overcame, and Beer describes the party as the unions' parliamentary committee.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should be able to affiliate to and help fund a political party.
missingStatements.rationale: The Labour Party began as a federation of unions with the TUC's parliamentary committee as its forerunner, and affiliated unions remained in the 1918 constitution.
missingStatements.declined: A narrow institutional detail of one party model; unions-good, collective-bargaining and independent-unions already capture the union side.

notes: The catalog entry redirects to Labour movement, a broader topic; this profile covers the labourist doctrine within it. Statements on gender, race, speech, religion and other new-politics issues were not addressed by the historic movement, so most are low-confidence inferences. Positions on foreign policy and defence were split between pacifist and Attlee-era wings.
